1: This question was well answered by the candidates. (a) This question was well answered with most candidates achieving full marks. The examiners were looking for hardware which was part of the laptop not added to it, like a mouse. (b) This question was well answered with many candidates achieving full marks, however there were many brand names given which cannot achieve marks. Most common correct answers were operating system, compiler and linker.
2: This was a well answered question. Most candidates were able to tick the bottom two answers correctly, namely ‘This printer uses an inked ribbon’ and ‘This printer uses tomography’.
3: (a) This question was quite well answered however the question asked for a description of the differences meaning that the answers required some detail in order to achieve the mark. (b) This question was well answered by many of the candidates. Many correctly referred to Bluetooth, the ‘cloud’ and email. There is a concern that candidates incorrectly answer USB as a device,
4: This question was well answered with many candidates achieving at least half of the available marks.
5: This question was fairly well answered by many of the candidates. There were some good answers with a range of methods described. Some candidates wrote about one method rather than a range of answers. The question asked for methods and therefore more than one method was needed to achieve the marks.
6: This was one of the best performing extended response questions with most candidates achieving four or more marks, showing a good understanding of health issues when referring to keyboards. As in previous years some candidates mixed up health issues and safety issues. There was a lot of repeated answers given with the first occurrence achieving the mark and the repeated answer not being assessed.
7: (a) Many candidates appear to have misread the question. Many candidates gave answers that were better for part (b). (b) In order to achieve good marks on questions like this one, candidates should relate their answer back to the scenario as well as giving detail. (c) Candidates gave a few good answers but many of the answers were vague. As with previous questions of this type in order to achieve marks candidates need to give more detail in their answers. Some candidates mixed up module with model.
8: (a) This was a well answered question with many candidates giving clear details on how to produce the bar chart. (b) Many candidates could describe the creation of a formula with the mouse well and achieved high marks on this question. However, some candidates forgot that the formula had to be produced by using a mouse, therefore answers relating to typing in the details achieved no marks. Some candidates were a little vague in their answers writing that data was entered, this could have been achieved by a mouse or a keyboard. (c) This was well answered question but there was confusion between ascending and descending and this is where candidates did not achieve marks.
9: Many candidates appeared to know the topic but were not able to explain it fully. Many candidates could give the name of the layer rather than describing it.
10: This question was quite well answered with many candidates achieving at least half of the available marks. (a) This was a very well answered question with many candidates achieving very high marks. Candidates were able to produce good designs that filled the available space. As in the previous examination series questions of this type which include labels need to be exact in the way they are spelt in relation to the question. (b) This was a well answered question. (c) Many answers lacked detail. When answering these description types of questions detail relating to the question is needed.
11: Parts (a) and (c) were well answered but some candidates gave ADC rather than DAC for part (b).
12: As principal examiner reports have stated for some time, discussion type questions need more detail than other types of questions. Many candidates gave answers that lacked this detail. Some candidates made good discussion points about censorship restricting viewpoints and not allowing people to have all the facts.
13: Some candidates could explain the term correctly, but many just repeated the question. Better answers included that a moderated forum is on a platform or a website rather than just the internet.
14: (a) This question was well answered with many candidates achieving good marks. Many candidates thought that firewall stopped hackers rather than devices. Some candidates wrote about the firewall protecting the internet. (b) Mostly good answers were given but quite a few explained how candidates could determine whether or not the information was reliable rather than why reliable information is not easy to find.
